newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Costa Rican president visits Aleman.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rican president visits Aleman.

text.p: Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres met Nicaragua's apparent president-elect Arnoldo Aleman on Saturday at Aleman's El Crucero estate on the outskirts of the capital Managua.

The quick visit was to show Costa Rica's support for Aleman in his disputed victory in Nicaragua's Oct. 20 presidential elections, which have been legally appealed as fraudulent by the left-wing Sandinista Front.
The final vote count gave Aleman a 51 percent to 37.7 percent win over Sandinista candidate Daniel Ortega.
Nicaraguan election authorities will rule on the appeal Nov. 20 and, barring a ruling in favour of the Sandinistas, Aleman will don the presidential sash Jan. 10.
Aleman told reporters it was an opportunity for him to get to know Figueres who "is the only Central American president I don't know."

Addressing the touchy issue of Nicaraguan illegal immigrants in neighbouring Costa Rica, Aleman said his government "would create employment so our best sons don't have to continue leaving the country." Thousands of Nicaraguans work illegally in the relatively wealthier Costa Rica, causing periodic diplomatic clashes over deportation of illegals and discrimination against Nicaraguans in Costa Rica.
Figueres returned to Costa Rica Saturday.
